tagline: Cameras, LiDAR, and IMUs lie in their own ways. I get them to agree.
bio: I spent five years shipping computer vision to production at Upjao Agrotech: detection models running on Jetson boards in the field, and the Kubernetes inference platform behind them. Now I'm doing an MS in Robotics at the University of Minnesota, building visual-inertial SLAM and Gaussian Splatting pipelines for ground robots.
focus: Fusing CLIP + DINOv2 into Gaussian splats for language-queryable 3D scenes
story: I started in Electronics & Communication Engineering at GITAM University, where signals, DSP, and probability gave me the math that perception still runs on. While I was still an undergrad, I joined the core team at Upjao Agrotech and started building computer vision for agriculture.

Over five and a half years there, I built the detection and segmentation models that graded agricultural produce on Jetson and Raspberry Pi boards, the serverless Triton and KServe platform that served them under 500ms, and a model-caching scheme that cut scale-up from 15–20 minutes to 3–4 seconds. That work turned into two granted patents and three more filed. Alongside it, I led a five-engineer team in TCS Rapid Labs that won the cohort's Best Team Award.

In 2024 I moved to Minneapolis for an MS in Robotics at the University of Minnesota to go deeper on the robotics side. As a graduate research assistant I build the ROS 2 mapping stack: a RealSense D435i feeding cuVSLAM for real-time visual-inertial SLAM, with Gaussian Splatting for reconstruction. At Parallax Worlds in San Francisco, I deployed that kind of reconstruction pipeline on Kubernetes across H100, A100, and T4 GPUs and cut processing time 30%.
I graduate in January 2027, and I'm looking for full-time roles in robotics perception, SLAM, and 3D vision.
